videos.title: BBNaija Winner Speaks - Luck, Hate, Love and Life After The House | Full Interview at The Beat FM
videos.headline: BBNaija Winner Speaks - Luck, Hate, Love and Life After The House | Full Interview at The Beat FM
videos.description:
In this exclusive exit interview, the BBNaija Season 11 finalists and evictees sit down to share their unfiltered truths about life inside the house and what happened after. Temi Nkem, the winner, opens up about being a gambit, feeling like the luckiest man, and why being emotional was never a weakness but a strength. She also addresses the disconnect between her UK accent and the core fan base, explaining that being Nigerian enough has nothing to do with how she speaks. The conversation then shifts to Sheba, who reflects on being the first female Head of House, dealing with age stereotypes, and the real root of her clashes with Tram: ideologies and the way we perceive things.

The housemates take turns revealing their next moves. Aikou talks about turning his imagination into books and music, while Barry shares his plans in fashion, punditry, and acting. Bluethopia gets candid about being misunderstood, her emotional strength, and her upcoming fashion brand. Ricky explains why he deliberately stirred chaos in the house and addresses the flirting with Sheba. Flora speaks on the difficulty of being a gambit and her beauty business goals. Oyin clears up misconceptions about performing for the cameras and reveals her jewelry and modeling plans. Tram discusses coming fifth, feeling appreciated, and his ambition to take over streaming globally. Temi Nkem also talks about driving in Nigeria, going back to school, and becoming a vlogger.

The interview wraps with Sheba explaining that her arguments with Tram were never about the surface issues but about deeper principles. Aikou shares his Abuja roots, Kogi heritage, and his vision for nationalism and Pan-African unity. This is a must-watch for every BBNaija fan who wants to know what really happened inside the Season 11 house and what these stars are planning next.

videos.headline: Producers Took Advantage Of Me - Nigerian Pornstar On Nollywood Exploitation & Why She Wants Out
videos.description:
She is speaking out. In this exclusive and eye-opening interview, a Nigerian adult film actress reveals the dark truth about the industry nobody talks about. From exploitation by Nollywood producers to making less than $50 for two million views, she holds nothing back. "I don't do it for passion. I just do it for survival."

She opens up about her journey into the industry, starting from Asaba Nollywood where producers took advantage of her. She talks about the stigma, the moral police, the depression and the reality that most people in this line of work are not making the millions they claim. "Most people are lying that they make huge amounts of money, which encourages others to join because they feel it is quick money. And it is not."

She also gets candid about safety, revealing she uses protection, is on PrEP and does her checkups every three months. But the emotional toll is heavy. Relationships are difficult. Friendships have been broken. She feels people only come close to take advantage of her. Yet she has found the strength to speak up and create awareness. "I've grown stronger. I have a thicker skin." She is now working her way out and focusing on her education and her passion for storytelling and entertainment. This is a must watch for anyone who wants to understand the real cost of survival.

videos.title: "You Have To Put Your Life In It" - Ladipoe Artistry, Talent & Why Artists Are Dodging Sacrifice
videos.headline: "You Have To Put Your Life In It" - Ladipoe Artistry, Talent & Why Artists Are Dodging Sacrifice
videos.description:
Ladipoe is not holding back. In this exclusive interview on the Morning Rush with Dreal Eve, he opens up about the real meaning behind "No Level" and why it should be the soundtrack to all your beefs. He talks about the people who pride themselves on being considerate and how sometimes you have to set boundaries. This song is for those who normally stay quiet. Now is your chance to speak up.

He also gets candid about the music industry and how things have changed. Discoverability is easier now with algorithms and platforms, but that does not mean talent is gone. It has just shifted to other places. He calls out lazy artists who are dodging the sacrifice it takes to be a real artist. For Ladipoe, you have to put your life in the music. That is what separates real artistry from just another income stream.

The conversation takes a personal turn when he talks about "Chosen" and the prayer his mother sent him. He cherished it for a long time and knew it had to be on that song. Where they are from, a mother's prayer is powerful. He also reveals his favorite songs on the album, including Palm Trees, Compose and Friend Indeed. And when asked who the hardest rapper in Nigeria is right now? His answer is simple. "Me. Period."

videos.title: EXCLUSIVE: Abi and Araga Spill On Nomy's Disqualification, HOH Pressure and Life After BBNaija
videos.headline: EXCLUSIVE: Abi and Araga Spill On Nomy's Disqualification, HOH Pressure and Life After BBNaija
videos.description:
Abi and Araga are out of the Big Brother Nigeria house and they are holding nothing back. In this exclusive interview, they open up about their journey from the first night to the final weeks. Abi, the first female Head of House twice, talks about the weight of the crown and how she had to switch her leadership style to keep the house together. Araga opens up about finding his circle, the friendships that mattered, and the moments that tested him.

Then the conversation turns to Nomy. Her disqualification. Did she deserve it? Did they see it coming? Abi says she figured it was going to happen. Araga says her attitude made it obvious. But the real bombshell comes when they are asked about their relationship with Nomy outside the house. Abi says she cannot be friends with someone who ignored her during a task and disrespected the team. Araga says he was never friends with her and does not see that changing. The friendship question gets a hard no from both.

They also talk about who they want to keep in their lives. Gerard and Yusuf are definite for Araga. Cassie gets a mention from Abi but she thought it was fake. Chimsom chuka never aligned. The house was a confined space and most relationships were just for show. Real life is different.

And they reveal their plans after the house. Abi wants to go to pilot school and make enough money to sponsor herself. Araga is a fashion model, actor, entrepreneur and athlete. He runs 100 and 200 meters and dreams of representing Nigeria. He also has an eyewear line called Araga that he has been building for four years.

videos.title: Fola Interview: Football Dreams, Davido/ Drake Dream Collab & Why He Believes Anything Is Possible
videos.headline: Fola Interview: Football Dreams, Davido/ Drake Dream Collab & Why He Believes Anything Is Possible
videos.description:
Fola is not your typical lover boy and he is setting the record straight. In this exclusive interview on the Midday show with Abi, he opens up about his new album, his approach to love songs and why he does not rush things anymore. "I know how to narrate love stories very well," he says. "I'm not much that deep of a lover boy like that."

He talks about his song My Type and how it is really a body positivity anthem. "Whatever sort of body type you have, you're beautiful just the way you are." He also speaks on his brotherhood with BNXN and whether an EP together is possible. "BNXN is my brother. Shout out to BNXN." He even reveals that he used to play football actively until he broke his arm. Would he have been a richer footballer than an artist? "I know how to sing more than I know how to play football."

The conversation gets deep when he talks about success and faith. "You can't tell me that nothing is impossible. That's just what I know." He believes Nigerians limit themselves and it is his responsibility to show people that anything can happen. He also reveals he would love a Fola and Drake song and has even written something for it. "When your dreams are too big, they laugh at you."

He also breaks down how 2am in Toronto came together. He recorded it a while ago, stumbled upon it in his archives while on tour in Canada, and reached out to OBO Baddest who picked it and sent it back the same night. The rest is history.
